prompt: A different client's automation reports 80% throughput, but they already run a monthly random sample of 100 automated cases checked against source documents, with results tracked separately from the throughput number. Does this setup have the same blind spot as the invoice example in the lesson?

options.text: Yes — any automation-rate metric has this blind spot regardless of what else is measured alongside it
No — an independent, ongoing sampled accuracy check is exactly what the lesson recommends adding, and this client already has one
Yes — monthly sampling isn't frequent enough to ever be considered a real validation checkpoint

hints: The lesson's fix wasn't 'never trust automation-rate numbers' — it was 'add an independent accuracy check.'
Check whether the missing piece from the invoice example — a sampled, independent correctness check — is present here.
explanation: The blind spot in the invoice example was the absence of any check independent of the automation-rate number itself — nobody was verifying correctness, only counting what skipped human review. This client already runs exactly the kind of ongoing sampled accuracy check the lesson recommends, tracked separately from throughput. The automation-rate number alone still wouldn't tell the whole story, but paired with the sampling process, the specific gap from the lesson doesn't apply here.
